positive.text:
I work in various stores around Tulsa. After spending a full 5 business days in the location at 21st and Garnett, I can say that this is one of the most enjoyable chains I've ever been to. And the community itself is just as amazing, treating me like a friend after just a few days.

Let me say first that i do not speak Spanish(my fault not theirs). The staff has been overwhelmingly accommodating. Either using translator apps or using what English they do speak to help me learn Spanish. They treated me almost like I'd been there for months instead of days and I will be making regular trips into Tulsa just to visit them more on my off time.

I did not see anyone being rude to any of the customers during my time there that were not rude or aggressive first. While i do not speak Spanish, my field has taught me how to listen to the tone that people use in conversation as much as the words. Their tones are almost always friendly until they're confused about trying to explain something in English and even then I feel as though they do their best.

My experience here was very good I like that they always have a large selection of fruits and vegetables. They also have a large selection of cheeses they have the full meat and Seafood counter. They also have a full pre-cooked kitchen area with a small seating area I have yet to try anything that I didn't like and I haven't tried everything.
PLENTY OF NATURAL FOODS, VEGETABLES,  A RESTAURANT INSIDE , EXCELLENT PLACE.

I stopped by looking for a glazed donut and a drink. This market has a lot going for it—a hot food section serving tacos and other Mexican dishes, a meat market, and a small bakery area. The store seemed well stocked and had a good variety of products.

My biggest issue was the customer service. Since most of the signage is in Spanish, I found myself a little lost trying to locate certain items. There were several employees around, and I walked near multiple staff members while they were stocking shelves, but nobody offered assistance or asked if I needed help.

The checkout experience wasn’t much better. After the cashier rang me up, she handed me my receipt and immediately turned around to talk to another employee. I had to stand there and ask for the drink I had just purchased because it was never handed to me. Only then did she give it to me.

I was curious about trying the taco section, but after this experience I didn’t feel very welcomed. The store has potential, but customer service and making customers feel acknowledged could definitely be improved.

Qué mala experiencia con esta tienda, de verdad. Un conocido mío que tiene diabetes se sintió muy débil e incluso llegó a desmayarse dentro del establecimiento. Lo más preocupante fue que las trabajadoras se negaron a llamar a una ambulancia, alegando que era por protocolo.

Me parece una situación vergonzosa y una falta de humanidad. Finalmente, el señor tuvo que ser hospitalizado. Considero que deberían revisar y cambiar sus protocolos para actuar adecuadamente en casos de emergencia médica. La salud y la seguridad de las personas deben estar por encima de cualquier procedimiento interno.

Ojalá no vuelva a ocurrir algo así. ¿Dónde queda la humanidad en situaciones como esta?

What a terrible experience with this store. A friend of mine who has diabetes became very weak and even fainted while inside the store. The most concerning part was that the employees refused to call an ambulance, claiming it was against their protocol.

I find this situation shameful and lacking basic human compassion. In the end, he had to be hospitalized. I strongly believe the store should review and change its policies so that employees can respond appropriately to medical emergencies. People’s health and safety should always come before any internal procedure.

I sincerely hope this never happens to anyone else. Where is the humanity in situations like this?
